regulatory_context: Government use of AI carries heightened scrutiny due to the power asymmetry between state and citizens, the impact on fundamental rights, and the requirement for democratic accountability. AI in public administration must meet higher standards of transparency, fairness, and due process. Many jurisdictions impose additional requirements on public sector AI beyond those applicable to private sector use.
key_regulators: National AI strategy bodies and offices

common_ai_use_cases.use_case: Benefits eligibility determination and social services allocation
common_ai_use_cases.risk_considerations: High-risk due to direct impact on vulnerable populations' access to essential services. Historical bias in training data may perpetuate systemic inequities. Requires robust appeals mechanisms and human oversight.

High-to-unacceptable risk. Potential for reinforcing discriminatory policing patterns, disproportionate surveillance of minority communities, and erosion of civil liberties. Some applications may be prohibited under EU AI Act.

Limited-to-medium risk for routine processing. Higher risk when automated decisions affect citizens' rights or entitlements. Must ensure accessibility and accommodate citizens who cannot interact with AI systems.
High-risk under EU AI Act Annex III. Biometric identification, risk profiling, and automated decision-making in migration contexts raise serious fundamental rights concerns.

best_practices: Publish algorithmic impact assessments for all AI systems used in public decision-making, with opportunity for public comment before deployment
Ensure all citizens affected by AI-assisted government decisions have access to meaningful human review and administrative appeals
Implement procurement standards that require AI vendors to demonstrate compliance with fairness, transparency, and accountability requirements
Conduct equity audits to verify AI systems do not disproportionately impact marginalized communities or perpetuate historical discrimination
Maintain public registries of AI systems used in government decision-making, including purpose, scope, and performance metrics

sector_specific_obligations.obligation: Conduct and publish algorithmic impact assessments before deploying AI systems that affect citizens' rights, benefits, or legal status
sector_specific_obligations.source: Canada AIDA / EU AI Act (Public Sector Provisions) / US Executive Order 14110

sector_specific_obligations.obligation: Ensure citizens have the right to human review of automated administrative decisions and provide clear information about how to exercise this right
sector_specific_obligations.source: Administrative Procedure Acts / GDPR Article 22 / EU AI Act Article 86

sector_specific_obligations.obligation: Prohibit or restrict use of AI for social scoring, mass surveillance, or real-time biometric identification in public spaces except under strictly defined legal exceptions
sector_specific_obligations.source: EU AI Act Article 5 / National constitutional protections
